answers.text: "elder_5d INTERRUPTED says force is fading, not resuming." elder is advisory only on my card, never a vote. My test is C5: D HH/HL, close 0.7% above the last swing high (42.96), W above EMA9 9>21. The H1 LH/LL is a minor swing my recording filters out (C21). I grant the break lacks follow-through (C17), so I wait for a new closing high; I do not concede the trend.

"Fresh high on day_vol 1.29 after a run: likely climax." My method reads a brand-new high as strength, not climax (C5, C16); a climax to me is a danger signal, a one-day fade from the high (C7), which has not printed. D HH/HL, 2.2% above the last swing high, 0.7% under the 20-day high. W LH/LL is the real caveat and keeps me at low conviction; no concession.

"No new high means wait for the break, not drop." This is my own test: W HH/HL 9>21, D HH/HL, 2.73% under the 79.8 pivot is an established trend in a normal reaction (C5, C8). My against was a not-yet, never a rejection; the right form of it is WAIT for close above pivot_high. Conceded on my own C5 terms.

"He buys the reaction; wait for value, not no entry." C5 forbids buying the reaction itself, so buying value on the pullback is not my entry. The W/D HH/HL grid is evidence I already granted; my entry stays the new high above pivot_high, never the dip. No concession on the method point.

decisions.reason: W HH/HL 9>21, D 0.8% under the 20-day high, H1 HH/HL above EMA9: trend column extending toward the new high (C5). D HH but LL and no second Financials name (C14) keep it modest.

decisions.reason: D HH/HL and 0.7% above the last swing high is the C5 new high after a pullback, but day_vol 0.39 and H1 LH/LL show no follow-through yet (C17): the extension must print first.

decisions.reason: W HH/HL 9>21 and D HH/HL, 2.73% under the 79.8 swing high: an established trend in a normal reaction (C8). C5 forbids the dip; the new high is the entry. mp DECELERATING keeps it a wait.
